reviewType: independent editorial review with sampled source verification

scope.notFullFactualVerification: All 100 bodies were read for unsupported universal/model applicability, replacement claims, unsafe instructions and obvious internal contradiction. Detailed source-row verification covered the 20 named samples only; the other 80 articles are not certified factually verified by this review. No manufacturer vehicle applicability join was independently re-established.

method: Read all 100 complete Markdown bodies, including scope and source paragraphs; reread the battery-monitor group after an initial aggregate output was truncated.
Compared the 20 named samples with full local primary-source text at exact physical PDF page boundaries, including continuation and neighboring pages where needed.

Visually inspected rendered original PDF pages gm-2025-03a 419 and 442 plus gm-2025-07a-2 743 to confirm command-state conflicts, event-count inequality and otherwise garbled driver/ohm glyphs. Poppler could not load libpoppler.so.160; PyMuPDF rendered the pages successfully.
Read-only review of articles and author metadata. Wrote only this report within the repository.

summary.conclusion: Suitable for draft integration with one citation-coverage correction. This is not publication approval or mechanic review. Existing unresolved-source flags must remain until their specific contradictions are resolved.

issues.title: Pressure-sensor mapping warnings omit the neighboring source pages that establish the conflict
issues.detail: Each article states a cross-row primary/secondary pulley naming contradiction, but its sourcePages metadata and footer cite only its own monitor row. The warnings are factually corroborated by this review; the problem is incomplete reader-visible support, not an invented mapping.
issues.recommendedCorrection: Add the relevant neighboring physical PDF page(s) to sourcePages and footer links. Keep the unresolved physical-mapping warning and needs-review status; do not select a pulley by assumption.

positiveFindings: No file-level make matrix was used as proof of per-code vehicle compatibility in the bodies reviewed.
Driver-state and pressure-versus-electrical distinctions remain explicit across relay, solenoid, pressure and converter families.
Sampled known source conflicts are disclosed rather than silently corrected; the PDF views confirm that the P0687 and P0E32 conflicts are in the source itself.
Converter articles do not infer hybrid/high-voltage architecture or prescribe hazardous internal probing from the generic DC/DC label.
